shorts.title: What you will learn: Range-based for
shorts.hook: Visit every item without a counter.
shorts.script: Visit every item without a counter. Today we loop without a counter. The range-based for visits every item for you, one at a time. A range-based for loop visits every item in a group. You do not need a counter, and you cannot go past the end. It works on strings, lists and many other groups. By default the loop variable is a copy. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Range-based for.

shorts.title: Range-based for in one minute
shorts.hook: A range-based for loop visits every item in a group.
shorts.script: A range-based for loop visits every item in a group. You do not need a counter, and you cannot go past the end. It works on strings, lists and many other groups. By default the loop variable is a copy. Add an ampersand to work on the real item. Think of a teacher calling the roll. Each name is called once, in order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Range-based for in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Word holds Konkani. The count starts at zero. The loop visits each letter. An if tests the letter against five vowels. A vowel adds one to the count. The word Konkani has three vowels, which are o, a and i. The program prints the count. The program prints Vowels colon three. A range-based for visits every item. You need no counter and no test. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Changing a copy
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in range-based for loops?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in range-based for loops? Bug of the Day. We try to change goa into capital letters. But the program prints goa again. The loop variable c is a copy. We change the copy and not the string. Add an ampersand after char. Then c is a nickname for the real letter. Without the ampersand, c is a copy of each letter. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Changing a copy.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you count the letter a in range-based for loops?
shorts.script: Can you count the letter a in range-based for loops? I wrote a for-each loop for my fish. Now every fish gets visited exactly once. Read a word. Use a range-based for to count how many times the letter a appears. Write your answer in the comments. A range-based for visits every item. You need no counter and no test. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
